correctness.rationale: Reflection averaging at one midpoint is valid for signed constant-preserving extensions. The two corner distance witnesses give affine lower bounds of opposite slopes, intersecting at L_a (or L_b), with positive minimizing weights. Transport to a vertex attains those bounds. For adjacent midpoints, convexity bounds the transport distance by the maximum of c,b,a,0: in the edge-to-edge case the common corner is fixed and the remaining half mass is sent diagonally. For opposite midpoints the uniform parts cancel. Thus the four operators fit together with midpoint-to-midpoint slopes at most one. Rationalizing D_a-D_b and using D_a+D_b≤3(a+b) identifies the controlling bound. The log of the positive excess over one is strictly concave in log t, and its derivative has opposite signs at the two ends. Independent bisection yields t=0.4115947538262989 and norm 1.0861565120461234. In RESULT.md line 45 the correspondences after squaring are reversed: b+c>D_a uses c>b, and a+c>D_b uses c>a. Both inequalities hold; the theorem and weights are unaffected.
residual_risks: The packaged 418 pair comparisons are finite floating-point evidence only. The proof is for positive side lengths, real scalar data and Euclidean chord distances.

value.rationale: The natural four-corner extension test distinguishes one-point obstructions from simultaneous ones. The result computes the exact unrestricted norm and shows positivity and no additional pairwise midpoint loss can attain it jointly. It also identifies which geometry is worst in the whole rectangle family, disproving the square as the worst aspect ratio.
residual_risks: No conclusion for general quadrilaterals or Banach-valued target data.
